title: KKR Buys 6% Stake in BookMyShow as India's Live Entertainment Market Booms
excerpt: The global investment firm's $40-50 million deal values India's largest ticketing platform at up to $833 million, as competition in the entertainment sector intensifies.
body:
• KKR is acquiring a roughly 6% stake in BookMyShow for $40-50 million, valuing the company at $667-833 million
  • The deal comes as India's live entertainment market surges, with BookMyShow hosting Coldplay, Ed Sheeran, and Travis Scott concerts
  • Competition is heating up as Walmart-owned Flipkart plans to enter ticketing and Eternal's District platform expands its presence
  • Founded in 2007 as a movie ticketing site, BookMyShow has evolved into a full-spectrum entertainment platform

KKR Places a Big Bet on Indian Entertainment

Global investment firm KKR will buy a stake of about 6% in Indian ticketing and entertainment platform BookMyShow for between $40 million and $50 million, according to Reuters, marking one of the most significant private equity moves in India's booming live entertainment sector.

The deal implies an estimated valuation of $667 million to $833 million for BookMyShow, a source told Reuters, requesting anonymity as they were not authorized to speak publicly. KKR declined to comment on the deal size, while BookMyShow did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

The companies announced the investment on Wednesday but did not disclose financial terms.

"We are seeing the opportunity in India's entertainment economy grow like never before."

— Ashish Hemrajani, Founder and CEO, BookMyShow

A Market Heating Up Fast

The investment arrives at a time of intensifying competition in India's entertainment-ticketing space. Walmart-owned Flipkart is planning to enter the events and ticketing market, while Eternal's District platform has been aggressively expanding its footprint, seeking a share of a market buoyed by robust demand for concerts, sports events, and live experiences.

Founded in 2007, BookMyShow has evolved well beyond its origins as an online movie ticketing platform. The company now operates as a broader entertainment company spanning films, live events, and immersive experiences. Its live entertainment division has hosted some of the biggest international acts to perform in India, including Coldplay, Ed Sheeran, and Travis Scott.

The platform's transformation mirrors a wider shift in Indian consumer spending. As disposable incomes rise and a young, urban population increasingly prioritizes experiences over material goods, the live entertainment industry has seen explosive growth. Concert attendance, sporting events, and theatre bookings have all surged in recent years.

KKR's Expanding India Portfolio

For KKR, the BookMyShow investment adds to a growing portfolio of bets on India's consumer economy. The New York-based firm has been among the most active private equity players in the country, backing companies across healthcare, financial services, and technology.

The deal also represents a significant reduction in size from earlier reported negotiations. In 2024, KKR was reportedly in talks to invest as much as $250-300 million in BookMyShow at a valuation of around Rs 7,500 crore. That deal was disrupted after Zomato acquired Paytm's entertainment ticketing subsidiaries for roughly Rs 2,048 crore, reshaping the competitive landscape and forcing a renegotiation.

The final deal — at roughly a fifth of the originally discussed investment — reflects both the changed competitive dynamics and a more cautious valuation approach in India's private markets.

What's Next

BookMyShow's path forward likely includes a public listing. The company turned profitable in fiscal year 2023, reporting a net profit of Rs 85 crore on operating revenue that nearly tripled to Rs 976 crore. With KKR now on the cap table alongside existing investors including Network18, Accel, and TPG Growth, an IPO could be the next logical step.

For India's entertainment economy, the deal underscores a broader truth: in the world's most populous nation, the business of going out is becoming serious business.
